To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the processing of the precursor transcripts and the expression of the subunit 1 of mitochondrial cyto-chrome c oxidase is altered in Syrian hamster cells initiated with ioniz- ing radiation, which is associated with increased levels of hydrogen peroxide and decreased cytochrome c activity.
ionizing radiation induces a neoplastic phenotype in Syrian hamster cells that is associated with alterations in the processing of mitochondrial cytochromec oxidase I precursor transcripts.
ionizing radiation can cause neoplastic conversion in Syrian hamster cells by altering the processing of mitochondrial transcripts and the levels of cytochrome oxidase I protein.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the molecular events that are responsible for the neoplastic transformation of mammalian cells.
the molecular alterations that are induced in Syrian hamster cells by ionizing radiations, and that are involved in their neoplastic conversion.
the molecular mechanisms underlying the initiation and progression of cancer.

radiation-initiated Syrian hamster fetal cell lines have increased levels of CO I mRNA and protein, and that these alterations may be involved in the neoplasia of these cells.

radiation-induced alterations in mt COI processing may be a key event in the neoplasia of mammalian cells.
